correctness.rationale: In the strict ceiling two, odd prefix heights must be one; even heights can be zero or two. This corrects frozen line 37, which says the intervening heights are always one or two. The internal pairs are exactly 10 or 01. An edge in the Dyck graph differs on full pair blocks and is Type A exactly when a consecutive block of equal orientations flips. XOR by the alternating mask turns these into alternating-interval flips; intervals of length at least two give the unrestricted two-read deletion graph and singleton flips give the cube, disjointly. One can check the Type-A criterion directly in the equal-content case: if deletions are at different positions, their alignment is a left or right shift on the first-to-last mismatch interval, and each orientation determines at most one descendant by shifting the deletion within equal runs to those two endpoints. Both orientations are possible exactly when the mismatches alternate; they then give distinct descendants. Counting intervals gives the degrees and edges including the empty bit vector. Trimming fixed endpoints preserves all Type-A adjacencies and sends the clique to the standard fixed-weight clique; the component coloring comes from the number of 01 pairs. Independent deletion-bucket enumeration through semilength eight checked the checksum, clique, constant-run graph, direct shortened deletion decks plus cube, degree maximum, edge totals and induced five-cycle. The all-parameter isomorphism is proved, not extrapolated.
residual_risks: The isomorphism is for height at most two, not higher ceilings. The coloring does not compute the largest single codebook.
